contentStrategy.searcherJob: Help an adult tabletop campaign player compare a dedicated AI game master with a general chatbot before choosing a solo RPG experience.
contentStrategy.readerStateBefore: The reader wants a solo tabletop campaign but cannot tell whether a dedicated AI game master offers more playable structure than a general chatbot.
contentStrategy.readerOutcome: The reader can compare action resolution, persistent campaign state, and voice-or-text play without relying on unsupported feature promises.
contentStrategy.primaryPainPoint: Generic AI roleplay pages blur the difference between prose conversation and a campaign system that interprets actions and retains RPG state.
contentStrategy.oneSentenceAnswer: Choose a dedicated AI game master when the job requires attempted actions, described outcomes, new choices, and persistent campaign state rather than open-ended chat alone.
contentStrategy.originalContribution: A decision framework that separates conversational fluency from the campaign jobs of interpreting actions, retaining state, and presenting consequential next choices.
contentStrategy.productBridge: Approved Playworlds facts describe a single-player voice-or-text AI adventure RPG with an AI game master, persistent campaigns, and tracked RPG state.
contentStrategy.contextualNextStep: After the comparison resolves the reader's decision barrier, offer one attributed visit to the official Playworlds Steam listing for current product details.
contentStrategy.evidenceBoundary: Public competitor and research sources establish the search task; only the approved Playworlds fact catalog may establish Playworlds capabilities.
contentStrategy.conversionHypothesis: A clear AI-game-master-versus-chatbot decision page should produce more qualified Playworlds outbound visits than a broad category explanation.
contentStrategy.measurementPlan: Measure the product-scoped qualified outbound by source slug and keep downstream trial, purchase, and revenue metrics unavailable until a verified Playworlds callback or an approved aggregate Steam model exists.
